name: אֲדֹנִי־בֶזֶק
summary: A Canaanite ruler whom Judah and Simeon found and fought at Bezek after Joshua’s death. He fled, was caught, and had his thumbs and great toes cut off, as he had done to seventy kings who gathered scraps under his table; he owned that God had repaid him, and died in Jerusalem. The name is אָדוֹן “lord” joined by ‑i to the name of his city: “lord of Bezek”, a title as much as a name, since the text meets him “in Bezek”.

evidence.note: וַיִּמְצְאוּ אֶת־אֲדֹנִי בֶזֶק בְּבֶזֶק, “they found Adoni-bezek in Bezek”: the lord of the place, in the place.
Judah struck ten thousand men at Bezek.
He fled; they caught him and cut off his thumbs and great toes.
“Seventy kings … gathered under my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me.”
אָדוֹן with a place: Shemer, אֲדֹנֵי הָהָר, lord of the hill.
Joseph, אֲדֹנֵי הָאָרֶץ, “the lord of the land”.

note: Written as two words without maqqef in Jdg 1:5–6 and with it in 1:7. The ‑i is read as the joining vowel (“lord of”), as Heb 7:2 reads the ‑i of מַלְכִּי־צֶדֶק; “my lord is Bezek” would need Bezek to be a god, of which there is no evidence. Bezek the place (Jdg 1:4; 1Sa 11:8) has no entry.
